source: សៀវភៅស្ដីពីដំណាំដំឡូងមី (Book on Cassava), Part 2, UNDP-supported capacity-building programme for cassava, March 2015, Section 8.2, citing CODEX STAN 176-1995
text:
The source presents the Codex Alimentarius international standard CODEX STAN 176-1995 for edible cassava flour, applying to flour made from fresh cassava root (Manihot esculenta Crantz) intended for direct human consumption. The flour is defined as a food product made by washing, peeling, grating/rasping, further processing, and drying fresh cassava root into dried flour/powder; where bitter cassava (Manihot utilisima Pohl, naturally higher in cyanogenic compounds such as linamarin) is used, additional detoxification steps are required.

Key quality/essential-composition requirements given:
- Moisture content: maximum 13% m/m (by weight). This limit is described as important for controlling storage conditions and preventing microbial/mold growth.
- Hydrocyanic acid (HCN) content: maximum 10mg/kg on a dry basis.
- General quality requirements: free of insect and other abnormal foreign-matter contamination; free of unnatural odor, color, or texture; free of visible mold.
- Contaminants: flour must be free of metal fragments or other physical contaminants; mycotoxin levels must comply with relevant Codex general contaminant limits for food products.
- Hygiene: production must follow Codex general principles of food hygiene (referenced in the source as CAC/RCP 1-1969, Rev. 2-1985) and relevant Codex Alimentarius contaminant standards.
- Food additives used, if any, must comply with the Codex General Standard for Food Additives (referenced as CODEX STAN 1-1985) as applicable to this product category.
- Labeling must follow the applicable Codex general standard for labeling of prepackaged foods.
- Recommended analysis methods cited include moisture determination per ISO 712-1998 and standard analytical methods for hydrocyanic acid content.
caveat: This is new, directly actionable export-standards content for the knowledge base, distinct from the agronomy-focused sources already covering cassava. The Codex standard number, moisture limit (13%), and HCN limit (10mg/kg) were read from a moderately clear source image; recommend a spot-check against the official CODEX STAN 176-1995 text if this figure will be used for compliance decisions, since standards can also be revised over time.
